stories.summary: A 70-page study released on Nov 25 by women's rights group Aware found that 87% of survivors surveyed who attempted to leave their abusers experienced continued abuse and control after separation — through withheld maintenance, using children as leverage, and dragging out legal proceedings. Aware called for a standalone offence covering repeated coercive and controlling behaviour, which is not currently criminalised in Singapore.
stories.title: Aware study: abuse often continues after separation for most survivors
stories.why: It puts hard numbers behind the push to criminalise coercive control in Singapore — leaving an abuser, the study shows, is often not the end of the abuse.

stories.summary: PlayStation 5 consoles are sold out islandwide after Grand Theft Auto VI made a record US$3.79 billion in first-day sales worldwide. Retailers say they field dozens of queries a day, Sony told one shopper restocks would come in January, and Xbox Series consoles are sold out too.
stories.title: PS5 sold out islandwide as GTA VI fuels console rush
stories.why: The biggest entertainment launch in years is hitting Singapore shelves directly — consoles are gone and no restock date is confirmed.

stories.summary: CNA found hundreds of listings for deregistered Singapore cars for sale in Johor Bahru, with some sellers admitting buyers drive them illegally using cloned plates. The cars, scrapped in Singapore, are being resold across the Causeway despite being unroadworthy and unregistered.
stories.title: Singapore scrap cars resold in JB — some driven illegally on cloned plates
stories.why: A cross-border enforcement gap is putting unregistered, uninsured cars back on the road — with safety and liability consequences on both sides of the Causeway.

stories.summary: Singapore's wholesale trade grew 14.5% in the third quarter of 2026 while retail sales fell 2.7%, according to the latest figures, a split picture even as the economy grew 6.1% in Q3 and the government raised its 2026 growth forecast to around 6%.
stories.title: Wholesale trade surges 14.5% while retail sales fall 2.7%
stories.why: The economy's two faces: business-to-business and AI-linked trade is booming while consumers pull back — a split worth watching into 2027.

stories.summary: Seatrium will cut about 220 jobs in Singapore — around 2% of its local workforce — as it consolidates yard work at Tuas Boulevard. Affected employees will get retrenchment packages plus job matching, career coaching and internal redeployment support.
stories.title: Seatrium to cut about 220 Singapore jobs in yard consolidation
stories.why: One of Singapore's big marine employers is shrinking its local headcount as it streamlines — a concrete sign of the yard consolidation now under way.

stories.summary: A New York jury convicted Huawei of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and of bank and wire fraud, acquitting it on racketeering and obstruction charges. Huawei said it plans to appeal, with sentencing set for 14 September.
stories.title: Huawei convicted of trade-secret theft conspiracy in US federal court
stories.why: A landmark verdict in the long-running US-China tech confrontation — a guilty verdict against one of China's flagship tech firms on trade-secret theft.

stories.summary: Dell beat third-quarter estimates, reporting adjusted earnings of $9.45 a share on $54.94 billion in sales, and guided above views, with shares rallying in extended trading. It also raised its fiscal 2027 AI-server revenue outlook to $78 billion as AI infrastructure demand stays strong.
stories.title: Dell smashes Q3 estimates and lifts guidance on AI server demand
stories.why: Even as AI stocks wobble, the hardware underneath the boom is still selling fast — Dell's AI server backlog is now the number to watch.

stories.summary: Jensen Huang told Nvidia staff at an all-hands meeting that he had violated parts of the company's code of conduct and made 'some terrible mistakes', a day after returning as CEO. He said he is in therapy and denied he was brought back because of pressure from President Trump. Nvidia shares fell about 6% on Tuesday, giving back part of Monday's 31.5% surge.
stories.title: Jensen Huang admits 'terrible mistakes' to Nvidia staff as shares slide 6%
stories.why: The CEO at the centre of the market's biggest story has now conceded the conduct breaches himself — while the stock gives back a chunk of its comeback rally.

stories.summary: Anthropic shares fell sharply in a renewed tech sell-off, closing just below $82 — under their $83 IPO price from the previous Thursday, only days after the company's record $81.3 billion float.
stories.title: Anthropic falls below its IPO price days after record float
stories.why: The largest IPO in history is already underwater — a measure of how fast sentiment has turned on the AI trade.

stories.summary: OpenTable agreed to acquire Australian restaurant-technology company me&u, which handles more than one million orders a week, to combine reservations with ordering and payments in a single platform.
stories.title: OpenTable to buy Australian restaurant-tech firm me&u
stories.why: Hospitality tech is consolidating in the region — bookings plus ordering and payments under one roof.

stories.summary: US stocks slid on Tuesday as the Nvidia relief rally fizzled: the Nasdaq fell 1.5% and the S&P 500 shed 0.5%, with Nvidia itself down almost 6% after Monday's 31.5% surge. The Dow closed higher, with Merck, Nike, Amgen and Salesforce among the gainers.
stories.title: US stocks slide as Nvidia rally fizzles out
stories.why: Monday's euphoria lasted exactly one session — the market is still hostage to the Nvidia story and to Fed hike bets.

stories.summary: Japan's Nikkei fell 2.8% on Wednesday, giving back much of Tuesday's 3.9% gain, as chip-related stocks led the decline — Advantest down 12% — after enthusiasm over Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia faded. The dollar was at 159.24 yen.
stories.title: Nikkei falls 2.8% as chip stocks drag Tokyo lower
stories.why: Asia's AI rally reversed within a day of its biggest gain in months — the same concentration that lifts the market is now dragging it down.

stories.summary: The dollar slipped on Tuesday, giving back much of Monday's gains, as the AI-stock rally sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement faded. The dollar index fell 0.52% to 103.76, with the euro up 0.72% at US$1.0978. Traders are pricing in 98% odds of a Fed hike in December.
stories.title: Dollar slips as Nvidia-fuelled AI rally fades
stories.why: The greenback's strong November is pausing as traders question how far the AI-driven growth story can run — and a near-certain December hike is already priced in.

stories.summary: British security officials have warned UK companies providing 'material support' to Ukraine's armed forces to brace for potential sabotage attempts by Russia, after a fresh wave of security incidents across Europe.
stories.title: UK warns defence suppliers to Ukraine over Russian sabotage
stories.why: The war's shadow campaign is reaching industry — firms supplying Ukraine are now being told to expect sabotage, not just cyberattacks.

stories.summary: Japan is drawing auto suppliers into its biggest military buildup since World War II, enlisting car-parts makers to speed rearmament against China, Russia and North Korea as Tokyo races to build up its defences.
stories.title: Japan draws auto suppliers into biggest arms buildup since WWII
stories.why: Tokyo is mobilising its car industry for rearmament — a structural shift in how Japan builds its military.

stories.summary: Canada's defence minister said Canada is sovereign and 'does not report to the US' after a Pentagon memo criticised its 'atrophied' defence capabilities and its review of the F-35 purchase, in a rare public rebuke between the close allies.
stories.title: Canada tells Pentagon it 'does not report to the US' after memo criticising its military
stories.why: A leaked Pentagon memo has triggered an unusually public spat over burden-sharing — exposing strain inside the US-Canada alliance.

stories.summary: Five people were killed after a Turkish Air Force AS-532 Cougar helicopter crashed during a training flight on Tuesday, the defence ministry said — the country's second fatal military helicopter accident in less than two weeks.
stories.title: Five killed as Turkish military helicopter crashes during training
stories.why: Two fatal crashes in 12 days raises questions about Turkish military aviation safety and maintenance.

stories.summary: Senior military officials from the Indian Army and the Chinese PLA held multi-day talks along the Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh, concluding the second round of corps commander-level talks on existing border practices. The discussions were described as cordial.
stories.title: India and China corps commanders hold second round of LAC talks in Arunachal
stories.why: The two armies are working through border practices in the eastern sector — quiet management of a standoff that still shapes Asia's security picture.

stories.summary: The US Navy marked a milestone for its first-of-its-kind Information Warfare Training Team Facility at Fort Story, Virginia — an advanced live, virtual and constructive training environment to prepare and certify information warfare personnel.
stories.title: US Navy marks milestone for first information warfare training facility
stories.why: The US Navy is formalising how it trains information warfare operators — a sign of how central the domain has become to modern conflict.

tldr: Singapore: Aware study finds abuse often continues after separation — 87% of survivors who tried to leave faced continued control.
Technology: Huawei convicted in a US court of trade-secret theft conspiracy, while Dell beats on AI server demand.
Finance: US stocks slide as the Nvidia rally fizzles and the dollar falls; the Nikkei drops 2.8%.
Defence: UK warns Ukraine defence suppliers to brace for Russian sabotage.
Information warfare: US Navy marks a milestone for its first information warfare training facility.
